decisions.statement: A refusal is a 429.
A refusal names the error type `rate_limit_error`.
A refusal has the anthropic error envelope.
A refusal names the eligible count against the total.
A refusal names the seconds a client is told to wait.
A pool with no known reset waits 60 seconds.
A reset at or behind the moment handed in waits 60 seconds.
A reset ahead waits the seconds up to that reset.
A wait of part of a second is rounded up to a whole second.
A wait never falls below one second.
A pool with no known reset says the earliest reset is unknown.
A known reset is said as an iso moment.
A response has the status text `Too Many Requests`.
A response is sent as json.
A response has the wait in a `retry-after` header.
The moment a wait is measured from is handed in.
Nothing here reads a clock.
Nothing here reads an account.
Nothing here writes a line.
The message a client reads is written in English alone.
A reset far ahead is answered a wait no client is expected to honour.

definition: the 429 a client is answered where every account is at its limit
